column5: Preconditions

column1: Verify the Work Order settings page shows all Simple-Flow toggles in order with new vs existing visually distinct
column5:
1. You are signed in as an Admin at https://sv7301.qa.shopview.com.
2. You can reach Administration.
column6:
1. Go to /administration/settings.
2. Click the 'Work Orders' tab.
3. Read the list of settings top to bottom.
column7:
1. The page lists these toggles: Auto-approve Lines, Require Vendor Invoice Number, Require Review Before Completion, Require Tech Story, Require Mileage, Require Engine Hours, Automatically Pick Inventory Parts.
2. Each toggle shows an On/Off control and its current state.
3. No 'operating mode' (Full/Simple) selector appears anywhere on the page.

column1: Verify there is no operating-mode selector and no VIN-required setting on the Work Order settings page
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
column6:
1. Scan the whole Work Orders settings tab.
2. Look specifically for a 'Mode' / 'Full vs Simple' selector.
3. Look specifically for a 'Require VIN' / 'VIN required' toggle.
column7:
1. There is no operating-mode (Full/Simple) selector.
2. There is no 'Require VIN' toggle in the Work Order settings.
3. Behavior is driven only by the individual setting toggles.

column1: Verify there is no 'Create Purchase Orders' toggle and the Vendor Invoice sub-setting always shows (POs always on)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
column6:
1. Look for a 'Create purchase orders' toggle in the Work Orders settings.
2. Locate the Vendor Invoice (Optional/Required) setting.
column7:
1. There is no 'Create purchase orders' toggle — purchase orders are always created for vendor parts (the Create-POs setting and the No-PO/Skip flow were retired).
2. The Vendor Invoice (Optional/Required) sub-setting always shows with its helper text.
column8: SV-7696 (Story 1 / §4 (Create-POs setting retired — POs always on))

column1: Verify the Require Vendor Invoice Number toggle is present with helper text and drives Optional vs Required completion
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
column6:
1. Locate the 'Require Vendor Invoice Number' toggle.
2. Read its helper text.
3. Note its current On/Off state.
column7:
1. The 'Require Vendor Invoice Number' toggle is present.
2. Helper text reads (approximately): 'When on, parts and a vendor invoice number are required to complete a work order. When off, complete now and receive parts later.'
3. Its state maps to requireVendorInvoiceNumber in GET /api/organizations/settings.

column1: Verify Auto-approve Lines ON approves a work-order line the moment it is added
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Auto-approve Lines is set to ON and saved.
3. An open work order is on its Lines tab.
column6:
1. Click New Line.
2. Fill in a canned line and Save.
3. Observe the new line's approval state.
column7:
1. The new line is created.
2. The line is immediately Approved.
3. No 'Needs Approval' / Approve-Decline prompt is shown for the line.

column1: Verify Auto-approve Lines OFF leaves a new line in Needs Approval with Approve/Decline actions
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Auto-approve Lines is set to OFF and saved.
3. An open work order is on its Lines tab.
column6:
1. Click New Line.
2. Fill in a canned line and Save.
3. Observe the new line's approval state and actions.
column7:
1. The new line is created.
2. The line shows a 'Needs Approval' state.
3. Approve and Decline actions are available on the line.

column1: Verify existing settings (tech story, mileage, engine hours, auto-pick) display the org's current values
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
3. GET /api/organizations/settings values are known for this org.
column6:
1. Read the Require Tech Story, Require Mileage, Require Engine Hours and Automatically Pick Inventory Parts toggles.
2. Compare each shown state against the API settings object.
column7:
1. Each existing toggle is shown.
2. Each toggle's On/Off state matches the org's current API value.
3. States display without altering the values.

column1: Verify first-use defaults on a brand-new org (auto-approve OFF, vendor invoice REQUIRED; no Create-POs setting)
column5:
1. A brand-new organization that has never edited Work Order settings is available.
2. Signed in as that org's Admin.
column6:
1. Open /administration/settings → Work Orders tab for the new org.
2. Read the default state of Auto-approve Lines and Vendor Invoice.
column7:
1. Auto-approve Lines = OFF (spec default — authoritative).
2. There is no Create Purchase Orders setting — purchase orders are always on.
3. Vendor Invoice = REQUIRED.

column1: Verify saving a settings change persists after page reload
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
3. Note the current state of one toggle (e.g. Require Engine Hours).
column6:
1. Flip one toggle (e.g. Require Engine Hours) to the opposite state.
2. Click Save Settings.
3. Reload the page.
4. Re-read the toggle. (Restore it afterward to leave the org unchanged.)
column7:
1. Save Settings completes without error (POST /api/organizations/settings/change).
2. After reload the toggle keeps the new state.
3. GET /api/organizations/settings reflects the new value.

column1: Verify a settings change applies to future completions only and not to already-completed work orders
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order was already completed under the previous settings.
3. You can change a Work Order setting.
column6:
1. Complete a work order under the current settings.
2. Change a relevant Work Order setting (e.g. Require Vendor Invoice Number) and Save.
3. Reopen the already-completed work order and inspect it.
column7:
1. The already-completed work order is not retroactively changed by the new setting.
2. Only work orders completed after the change follow the new setting.

column1: Verify a non-admin user cannot see or modify the Work Order settings
column5:
1. A user without the App Settings permission (e.g. Service Advisor or Technician) exists for this org.
2. You can sign in as that user.
column6:
1. Sign in as the user without App Settings.
2. Attempt to open /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
3. Attempt to change and save a Work Order setting, including a direct API save.
column7:
1. A role without the App Settings permission cannot reach the Work Order settings, or sees them read-only.
2. That role cannot save changes to Work Order settings.
3. The backend rejects a Work Order settings save attempted by a role that lacks App Settings.

column1: Verify the settings model contains no operatingMode field and no requireVin setting
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin with API access.
2. You can call GET /api/organizations/settings.
column6:
1. Call GET /api/organizations/settings.
2. Inspect the returned object keys for 'operatingMode'.
3. Inspect for a 'requireVin' Work Order setting.
column7:
1. There is no operatingMode field in the settings object.
2. There is no requireVin Work Order setting exposed.
column8: SV-7696 (S1 AC (no requireVin / no operatingMode field))

column1: Verify the Save Settings button is only enabled when there is an unsaved change
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab with no pending changes.
column6:
1. With no changes made, look at the Save Settings button.
2. Flip a toggle and look at the Save Settings button again.
column7:
1. Saving persists the settings changes.
2. Dirty-state gating (disabling Save until a change is made) is NOT required in v1 — Save being always enabled is acceptable (low-priority polish, not a blocker).

column1: Verify the Require Review Before Completion toggle is present on the settings page and drives the review flow
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
column6:
1. Locate the 'Require Review Before Completion' toggle.
2. Turn it On and Save.
3. Start completing a work order and observe the completion CTA.
column7:
1. The 'Require Review Before Completion' toggle is present on the page (not prototype-only).
2. With it On, completing a work order routes into the review flow (Story 16).
3. The completion CTA relabels to 'Complete & Send to Review'.

column1: Verify every Work Order setting toggle has descriptive helper text
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
column6:
1. Read each toggle's supporting description text.
2. Confirm each explains what On vs Off does.
column7:
1. Every toggle has a short helper description.
2. Each description explains the On and Off behavior in plain language.

column1: Verify a Complete Work Order button appears next to New Line on the work order
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. An open work order with at least one approved line is on its Lines tab.
column6:
1. Look at the work order Lines toolbar.
2. Locate the New Line button.
3. Locate the Complete Work Order button.
column7:
1. A 'Complete Work Order' button is present.
2. It sits near the New Line action on the work order.
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699 (Story 3/4 (streamlined completion — Complete button placement))

column1: Verify a work order with no parts completes in one confirm and reaches the Success screen
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. An open work order with a single labor-only, approved line exists (no parts).
3. Required-field settings for this org are known (e.g. Require Mileage ON).
column6:
1. On the work order Lines tab, click Complete Work Order.
2. If a tech-story modal appears first, enter a story and click Continue.
3. In the Details step, enter any required fields (e.g. Mileage).
4. Click Complete Work Order in the wizard.
column7:
1. There is no PO / receive / invoice step for a no-parts work order (wizard = Details → Success).
2. The Success screen appears reading 'Order complete' and 'Sent to Finance as an invoice-ready draft'.
3. All lines move to Completed and the work order status becomes Complete.
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699 (Story 3/4 (streamlined completion — no-parts WO one-confirm))

column1: Verify the Success screen shows the work order number and total with Done and Go to Invoice actions
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You have just completed a work order and are on the Success screen.
column6:
1. Read the work order number on the Success screen.
2. Read the total shown.
3. Identify the Done and Go To Invoice buttons.
column7:
1. The Success screen shows the work order number (e.g. S2-15747).
2. It shows the invoice total (e.g. $382.77).
3. Both a Done and a Go To Invoice button are present.
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699, SV-7710 (Story 3/4 (streamlined completion — Success screen) / S15-R3)

column1: Verify Go to Invoice from the Success screen opens the Finance step where the invoice number is shown
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are on the Success screen of a just-completed work order.
column6:
1. Click Go To Invoice.
2. Observe the destination screen.
3. Look for the invoice number.
column7:
1. You are taken to the Finance / invoice step for that work order.
2. The invoice number is shown on the Finance step (not on the Success screen).
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699, SV-7710 (Story 3/4 (streamlined completion — Go to Invoice) / S15-R3)

column1: Verify completion is blocked when a required vehicle field is missing
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Mileage (or another required field) is ON.
3. An open work order with an approved line and NO mileage recorded is ready to complete.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. In the Details step, leave the required field (e.g. Mileage) empty.
3. Attempt to confirm completion.
column7:
1. Completion is blocked while the required field is empty.
2. The user is prompted to supply the missing required field.
3. Completion proceeds only after the required field is filled.
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699 (Story 3/4 (streamlined completion — missing required fields blocked))

column1: Verify a work order with a vendor part creates a PO on completion and routes through the receive step (POs always on)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. An open work order with an approved vendor-part line exists.
3. POs are always on — there is no Create-POs setting to turn off.
column6:
1. Start completion of the work order.
2. Observe whether a PO / background order is created for the vendor part and whether receiving is required.
3. Complete after receiving and check the vendor bill / AP sync.
column7:
1. A PO (background order) is created for the vendor part; Complete Work Order stays disabled until the part is received (S4-R1/R4).
2. After receiving, completion proceeds and the vendor bill / AP sync occur per the normal pipeline.
3. There is no skip/no-PO path — the former Create-POs-OFF flow was retired.
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699 (Story 3/4 (POs always on — former Create-POs-OFF flow retired))

column1: Verify in-stock inventory parts decrement inventory and write Part History on simple completion
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. An open work order has an approved in-stock inventory part line.
3. Note the part's current on-hand quantity.
column6:
1. Complete the work order via the simple (skip) flow.
2. Check the inventory on-hand quantity for that part.
3. Check the part's Part History.
column7:
1. The in-stock part's on-hand quantity decrements by the used amount.
2. A Part History entry is written for the movement.
3. The skip path does not bypass inventory movement / Part History.
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699 (Story 3/4 (streamlined completion — inventory movement) / §5 invariant 1)

column1: Verify with Auto-pick Inventory OFF the completion modal requires picking parts before Complete
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Automatically Pick Inventory Parts is OFF and saved.
3. An open work order with an approved inventory-part line exists.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Observe the Pick step in the completion modal.
3. Try to continue without picking, then pick and continue.
column7:
1. A Pick step appears offering 'Pick all from default bins' and 'Review individually'.
2. You cannot complete until inventory parts are picked.
3. After picking, completion can proceed.
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699 (Story 3/4 (streamlined completion — auto-pick off ⇒ pick in modal))

column1: Verify adding a new line to a completed work order returns it to Approved
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order is in Complete status.
column6:
1. Open the completed work order.
2. Add a New Line.
3. Observe the work order status.
column7:
1. The work order status returns to Approved.
2. On the next completion, the modal summarizes already-received vs newly-added parts.
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699 (Story 3/4 (streamlined completion — re-open returns to Approved))

column1: Verify individual-line Complete and per-part receive actions still work alongside Simple completion
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. An open work order with multiple lines and a receivable part exists.
column6:
1. Complete one individual line on the work order.
2. Perform a per-part receive action on a line's part.
3. Confirm the line-level Receive button is present.
column7:
1. An individual line can still be completed on its own.
2. The existing per-part receive action still works.
3. A line-level Receive button remains available.
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699 (Story 3/4 (streamlined completion — individual-line Complete + per-part receive))

column1: Verify the optional-invoice completion wizard offers Receive Parts, Complete Without Receiving and Cancel
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Vendor Invoice Number is OFF (Optional).
3. An open work order with an approved part-bearing line exists.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Observe the wizard actions.
column7:
1. The wizard shows a Receive step (e.g. 'N parts waiting to receive').
2. The actions are Cancel, Complete Without Receiving, and Receive Parts.

column1: Verify the optional-invoice modal creates POs in the background and shows the count of parts to receive
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Vendor Invoice Number is OFF (Optional).
3. An open work order with two approved vendor-part lines exists.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Read the parts-to-receive count in the modal.
3. Check that POs were created in the background for the vendor parts.
column7:
1. The modal shows the number of parts waiting to receive (e.g. '2 parts waiting to receive').
2. Background POs are created for the vendor parts (a vendorless / sell-price-only part goes on the work order's PO flagged Vendor Missing).
3. All approved-line parts are actually ordered and reach waiting-to-receive, so 'Receive Parts' always has something to receive.
4. No approved part is left in 'requested' and routed to an empty receive screen.
5. Inventory-pick status is reflected in the modal.

column1: Verify Receive Parts opens the shared Accept Delivery page to receive all vendors at once
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are in the optional-invoice completion wizard for a multi-vendor part work order.
column6:
1. Click Receive Parts.
2. Observe the destination screen.
3. Confirm all vendors' parts appear together.
column7:
1. The shared Accept Delivery page opens.
2. Parts from all vendors are shown for receiving at once.

column1: Verify Complete Without Receiving completes the WO, keeps unreceived parts waiting, and keeps the line Receive button
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are in the optional-invoice completion wizard with unreceived parts.
column6:
1. Click Complete Without Receiving.
2. Observe the work order status and the Success screen.
3. Reopen the work order and check the unreceived part lines.
column7:
1. The work order completes and the Success screen appears.
2. Unreceived parts remain in a waiting-to-receive state (would show in the Waiting on Parts column).
3. The line still shows a Receive button.

column1: Verify Cancel closes the completion modal with no change and no duplicate POs on re-open
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are in the optional-invoice completion wizard (POs already created in the background).
column6:
1. Click Cancel.
2. Reopen the completion wizard by clicking Complete Work Order again.
3. Check the POs for the work order.
column7:
1. Cancel closes the modal with no change to the work order.
2. Re-opening and re-completing does not create duplicate POs (idempotent).

column1: Verify the optional-invoice modal collects required vehicle fields (mileage, VIN, engine hours) when missing
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Mileage / Engine Hours are ON and the work order is missing those values.
3. You are completing a part-bearing work order with invoice Optional.
column6:
1. Start completion.
2. Observe the required vehicle fields collected.
3. Leave one empty and try to continue.
column7:
1. The modal collects the required vehicle fields that are missing.
2. Continuation is blocked until required fields are supplied.
3. Tech story is handled separately (Story 17), not inside this step.

column1: Verify the optional-invoice flow reaches the Success screen with WO number and total
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You completed a part-bearing work order via Complete Without Receiving (invoice Optional).
column6:
1. After completing, read the Success screen.
2. Identify the WO number, total, and Go to Invoice / Done buttons.
column7:
1. The Success screen shows the WO number and total.
2. Go to Invoice and Done are available.

column1: Verify the required-invoice wizard disables Complete until parts are received and offers no skip option
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Vendor Invoice Number is ON (Required).
3. An open work order with two approved unreceived part lines exists.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Observe the primary CTA state.
3. Look for a 'Complete without receiving' option.
column7:
1. The wizard shows a Receive step ('2 parts waiting to receive').
2. The primary Complete Work Order CTA is DISABLED until all parts are received.
3. There is NO 'Complete without receiving' option.
4. Approved sell-price-only parts (missing vendor and/or cost) are ordered too and reach waiting-to-receive before the receive gate — no approved part is left in 'requested' with nothing to receive.

column1: Verify the required-invoice receive round-trip returns to the modal and enables Complete once all received
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are in the required-invoice completion wizard with unreceived parts.
column6:
1. Click Receive Parts.
2. On the shared Accept Delivery page, enter qty, tax, date, note and vendor invoice # per vendor and receive all parts.
3. Click Back to Work Order (or finish).
4. Observe the completion modal CTA, then click Complete Work Order.
column7:
1. The receive page collects qty, tax, date, note and invoice # per vendor.
2. On return, once all parts are received the Complete Work Order CTA is enabled.
3. Completing shows the Success screen.
4. Sell-price-only parts were ordered to waiting-to-receive, so they appear in the receive round-trip and are not left in 'requested'.

column1: Verify Cancel in the required-invoice wizard makes no change to the work order
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are in the required-invoice completion wizard.
column6:
1. Click Cancel.
2. Inspect the work order status and lines.
column7:
1. The modal closes.
2. The work order is unchanged (still not completed).

column1: Verify completing a work order with an unapproved line shows the approve-line error and does not complete
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Auto-approve Lines is OFF.
3. A work order has one line still in Needs Approval and all other gates satisfied (tech story present, required fields present).
column6:
1. Open the work order with one line in Needs Approval and all other gates satisfied.
2. Look at the Complete Work Order button and hover it for any tooltip.
3. Approve the remaining line and re-check the button.
column7:
1. The Complete Work Order button is disabled while any line is unapproved.
2. A tooltip on the disabled button describes the reason (which line needs approval).
3. The button enables and completion proceeds once all lines are approved (S4-R8).
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699 (Key Decision (all lines approved) / S3-R9 / S4-R8)

column1: Verify a manually unapproved line still blocks completion even when Auto-approve is ON
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Auto-approve Lines is ON.
3. A work order has a line that was manually un-approved after being added.
column6:
1. Confirm one line is unapproved (manually un-approved after being added, Auto-approve ON).
2. Look at the Complete Work Order button (disabled) and its tooltip.
3. Re-approve the line and retry.
column7:
1. With the line unapproved, the Complete Work Order button is disabled with a tooltip describing the reason.
2. After re-approving all lines, the button enables and completion proceeds (holds regardless of Auto-approve).

column1: Verify re-running completion after a prior attempt does not create duplicate POs
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A part-bearing work order already had completion started once (POs created).
column6:
1. Cancel or exit the first completion attempt.
2. Start completion again.
3. Inspect the POs for the work order at /parts/orders.
column7:
1. Only one PO per vendor exists.
2. No duplicate POs are created by the second completion attempt.

column1: Verify inventory cores are resolved via a line-level Ok/Not-OK control (no distinct Resolve-Cores wizard step)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has an approved inventory line that carries a core charge.
3. Auto-pick is set so the Pick step runs (or picking is otherwise required).
column6:
1. Add a cored inventory part to a work order line and open the line's Parts view.
2. Confirm the part generates a Core sub-line with per-core Ok / Not-OK controls and a $ amount.
3. Click Complete Work Order and step through the completion wizard.
4. Confirm there is no distinct Resolve Cores step and completion goes Details -> Success.
column7:
1. The cored part generates a Core sub-line on the line's Parts view with per-core Ok (returned, no charge) and Not-OK (keep + charge) controls and a $ amount ($0 until Not-OK).
2. The completion wizard has NO distinct Resolve Cores step; a work order whose only remaining action is core resolution completes Details -> Success.
3. Core resolution is a line-level control, not a wizard step.
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699, SV-7870 (S3-C1 / S4-C1 / Resolve Cores handoff)

column1: Verify a work order with no cores completes with no core sub-lines and no Resolve-Cores wizard step
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has no core parts.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Step through the completion wizard.
3. Watch for a Resolve Cores step.
column7:
1. No core sub-lines appear (the work order has no cores).
2. There is no distinct Resolve Cores wizard step; completion proceeds directly Details -> Success.

column1: Verify special-order cores leave the optional-invoice completion unchanged and Complete Without Receiving stays available
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Vendor Invoice Number is OFF (Optional).
3. A work order has a special-order (vendor) cored part not yet received.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Observe whether a core-resolution step appears.
3. Confirm Complete Without Receiving is still available.
column7:
1. There is nothing to resolve yet for special-order cores in the completion modal.
2. Complete Without Receiving remains available.

column1: Verify the invoice shows a 'Cores pending' flag when unresolved special-order cores exist
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A completed (optional-invoice) work order has an unresolved special-order core.
column6:
1. Open the work order's invoice / Finance view.
2. Look for a cores indicator.
column7: 1. The invoice shows a 'Cores pending' flag while special-order cores are unresolved.

column1: Verify resolving cores at the Create Invoice gate routes to receive the cored line then lets invoicing proceed
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A completed (optional-invoice) work order has an unresolved special-order core.
column6:
1. Click Create Invoice.
2. In the resolve module, route to receive the cored line (core-only partial receive).
3. Resolve each core Ok / Not OK.
4. Continue to invoice.
column7:
1. The Create Invoice gate opens a resolve module for the unresolved cores.
2. It routes to receive the cored line(s) (core-only partial receive supported).
3. After resolving Ok/Not OK the invoice proceeds.

column1: Verify cancelling the invoice-gate core resolution leaves the WO completed, un-invoiced and cores-pending
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A completed work order has an unresolved special-order core and you are in the invoice-gate resolve module.
column6:
1. Cancel the resolve module.
2. Inspect the work order and invoice state.
column7:
1. The work order remains Completed.
2. It remains un-invoiced.
3. Cores remain pending.

column1: Verify special-order cores are resolved after the required-invoice Receive round-trip before Complete
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Vendor Invoice Number is ON (Required).
3. A work order has a special-order cored part.
column6:
1. Complete Work Order → Receive Parts and receive the cored part.
2. On return, observe the Resolve-cores modal.
3. Resolve each core Ok / Not OK, then Complete.
column7:
1. After the receive round-trip a gated Resolve-cores modal appears.
2. Cores can be resolved (part is always received, so always resolvable).
3. After resolving, Complete succeeds to the Success screen.

column1: Verify the invoice gate detects an unresolved special-order core that exists only as a PartRequest
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A completed work order has a special-order cored part that exists only as a PartRequest (no WorkOrderPart yet).
column6:
1. Click Create Invoice.
2. Observe whether the unresolved core is detected.
column7:
1. The invoice gate detects the unresolved core even though it is only a PartRequest.
2. The user is required to resolve it before invoicing.

column1: Verify a vendorless part can be requested with description, quantity and category (part number, cost, vendor and sell price left empty)

column1: Verify permission gating of Simple-Flow settings and work-order actions (UI gating is the v1 pass criterion)
column5:
1. Signed in with API access.
2. A relevant Simple-Flow setting (e.g. Require Vendor Invoice Number) is ON.
column6:
1. As a role that lacks the mapped permission, confirm the gated setting/action is hidden or unavailable in the UI.
2. Attempt the same setting change directly via the API (bypassing the UI) as that role, and note the response.
3. As a role that lacks the completion / review sign-off permission, attempt to complete a work order and to sign off a review directly via the API, and note the response.
4. As a role that has only Work Orders: Create & Edit, attempt to receive onto a work order and note the response.
column7:
1. UI gating is the pass criterion for v1: a role without the mapped permission does not see or cannot use the gated setting/action in the UI.
2. The Simple-Flow settings atom is enforced at the backend too — the unauthorized settings request is rejected.
3. The work-order completion and review sign-off atoms are NOT enforced at the backend — a direct API call from a role lacking the permission still succeeds. This passes for v1 on the UI restriction, but the API-level gap is a KNOWN ISSUE to fix; record the result as 'UI pass / API fail' so it stays on record.
4. Because several work-order atoms collapse to the same backend role pair, any role with Work Orders: Create & Edit can receive onto / act on a work order via the API (documented OR of ROLE_DELIVERY_CREATE_AND_EDIT, ROLE_WORK_ORDER_PART_CREATE and ROLE_WORK_ORDER_CREATE_AND_EDIT).
